walkthroughs.body_html:
Decision Making to Improve Human Resource Performance — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Decision Making to Improve Human Resource Performance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Decision Making to Improve Human Resource Performance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A firm with 200 staff has 20 leavers this year. Its labour turnover is:
Which of the following is a measure of labour productivity?
options: Output per employee per time period
Total revenue divided by total costs
Leavers divided by average staff employed
Days absent divided by total working days

mcqs.q: A wider span of control means:
options: Each manager is directly responsible for more subordinates
The business has more levels of hierarchy
Decision-making is fully centralised
Each employee reports to more managers
Removing levels of management from the hierarchy
Recruiting additional supervisors
Moving production to another country
Splitting the business into separate companies

mcqs.q: Does a high labour turnover always indicate poor management?
options: Any labour turnover is bad and should be reduced to zero.
Pay is illegal to use as a motivator under UK law.
Labour turnover measures how quickly stock is sold.
Not necessarily — some turnover brings fresh ideas and skills, and rates vary by industry; but persistently high turnover raises recruitment and training costs.

mcqs.q: Is paying workers more the best way to motivate them?
options: Not always — Herzberg argued pay mainly prevents dissatisfaction as a hygiene factor, while motivation comes from the work itself, recognition and responsibility.
Delayering means redesigning the office floor layout.
Pay is illegal to use as a motivator under UK law.
Higher pay always produces proportionally higher motivation and productivity.

mcqs.q: Does delayering always improve HR performance?
options: Removing management layers always makes a business more efficient.
No — it cuts costs and speeds communication, but it widens spans of control, can overload remaining managers, and may damage morale and promotion prospects.
Labour turnover measures how quickly stock is sold.
Delayering means redesigning the office floor layout.
